newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tchibo, Eduscho would have 30.2 percent mkt share.
newsitem.headline: Tchibo, Eduscho would have 30.2 percent mkt share.

text.p: German coffee roaster Eduscho GmbH & Co KG and Tchibo Holding AG, if they merged their coffee interests, would have a combined German roasted coffee market share of 30.2 percent, according to Tchibo.
Eduscho announced earlier on Wednesday Tchibo was intending to buy the Bremen-based company as of January 1, 1997, pending cartel authority approval.
Tchibo spokesman Matthias Born said the 30.2 percent figure -- made up of Thciob's 19.8 percent and Eduscho's 10.4 -- applied to current volume market shares, which fluctuated.

But the two would overtake current market leader Jacobs Cafe, the coffee arm of Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), part of the U.S. Philip Morris food group, which in the summer of 1996 reported a market share of 27.3 percent.

Born would not comment on the intended purchasing price, chances of approval or the expected decision time, as this would presuppose approval and could spoil Tchibo's chances of securing the deal, he said.
Similarly, he could not specify what the two companies were planning for their relevant chains of tied retail outlets, which sell coffee and consumer goods.
Tchibo coffee sales in 1996 were estimated at 3.50 billion marks and Eduscho's at 2.25 billion, Tchibo said.
Tchibo has 6,200 employees, of which 4,800 were based in Germany. It operates in Germany, Poland, the Czech and Slovak republics, Hungary, Austria, and the Netherlands.
Eduscho employs 5,250, of which 3,950 are domestic. It operates in Germany, the Slovak republic, Hungary and Austria.
